title: AI-Assisted Smart and Efficient Radio Access Networks
summary: IIT Gandhinagar proposes learned traffic forecasts and GNN/DRL policies to support adaptive routing, alongside conventional network optimization.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: The framework combines learned traffic prediction and a proposed graph-neural-network/deep-reinforcement-learning policy with classical routing optimization. The intended AI contribution is better anticipation of demand and more adaptive routing decisions. Simulation and evaluation are planned. Operator energy savings attributable to AI remain unreported.
purpose: Use learned demand forecasts and routing policies to allocate network resources efficiently.
system: AI-Assisted Smart and Efficient Radio Access Networks

ratings.reason: More efficient routing through learned forecasts and policies is intended; no attributable operator energy or throughput improvement is reported.
Lower emissions resulting from AI-assisted network decisions remain intended.

ai_role.statement: Traffic models predict demand; GNN/DRL policies are proposed for adaptive decisions in larger networks.

evidence.citation: International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025). Project-submitted account, current as of June 2025. ITU provides no independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Use Case 11: AI-Assisted Smart and Efficient Radio Access Networks

produced_by: The account does not establish conditions sufficient to reproduce the benefit.
must_hold: The account does not establish requirements for reproducing the benefit in other settings.

headline: Learned traffic prediction aims to improve network routing
claim_basis: Sources: the makers' report. The cited evidence includes no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
